div.p: Each PersonalRelationship resource records a single, unidirectional relationship between two individuals. If the inverse relationship also needs to be recorded, it is represented by a separate PersonalRelationship resource. Properties such as confidence, period, and asserter are recorded independently and can differ between the two directions.

Some relationship types imply an inverse relationship, but do not determine its most specific type. For example, "father of" implies "child of", but does not establish whether the child is a son or daughter. Likewise, "child of" implies "parent of", but not specifically mother or father. Recording one direction does not automatically create a PersonalRelationship resource for the inverse direction.
The family relationship examples use Patient resources for Jane, John, and Mary, and three separate PersonalRelationship resources:

li.a: Mary (source) is the daughter (relationshipType) of Jane (target).
Jane (source) is the mother (relationshipType) of Mary (target).
Mary (source) is the daughter (relationshipType) of John (target).

div.p: Each PersonalRelationship describes only one direction. The daughter and mother relationships between Mary and Jane are recorded explicitly, rather than relying on an inferred inverse. Confidence applies only to the relationship on which it is recorded; omitting it does not assert certainty.
